domains.original: Arbitrary measurable spaces, s-finite μ,R,F; no normalization or finiteness of total mass; zero measures, empty spaces, infinite fluxes allowed.
domains.reconstructed: Arbitrary sigma-algebras with product sigma-algebra on A×B, countable-sum s-finiteness, no nonemptiness/countability/separation/topology/probability/finite-mass premise; fluxes in [0,∞].
domains.evidence: Candidate binders are exactly {A B : Type*}, [MeasurableSpace A], [MeasurableSpace B], [SFinite μ], [IsSFiniteKernel R], [IsSFiniteKernel F]. No other local/scoped premises occur in the whole module. Defs.lean:153–155,346–348 defines s-finite kernels as countable sums of uniformly bounded finite kernels, not mere fiberwise s-finiteness. MeasureCompProd.lean:183–186 and Prod.lean:130–134 give genuine formulas under these classes; no zero-default behavior outside them is used.

quantifiers.original: For arbitrary A,B,μ,R,F, assume that for μ-almost every a the fiber kernel is reversible, i.e. has balance for every pair of measurable fiber sets; conclude joint reversibility.
quantifiers.reconstructed: One μ-null exceptional set, independent of measurable E,G; outside it all fiber balances hold. Joint conclusion ranges over every measurable U,V⊆A×B.
quantifiers.evidence: hF is ∀ᵐ a ∂μ, IsReversible(F_a)(R a), with IsReversible's ∀ measurable sets inside the a.e. quantifier (Invariance.lean:60–62). It is not ∀ E,G, a.e. a with pair-dependent exceptions. Proof filter_upwards [hF] selects one good a before applying ha to its S_a,T_a. The public theorem starts intro S T hS hT, so conclusion is not rectangle-only.

assumptions.original: μ,R,F are s-finite; F is jointly measurable; fibers have μ-a.e. detailed balance under the same R(a). No normalization/finite-mass premise.
assumptions.reconstructed: The same s-finite genuine kernel assumptions and simultaneous a.e. detailed-balance premise; no Markov, density, real-integrability, Standard-Borel or measurable-singleton assumption.
assumptions.evidence: Every public binder has source or typing justification. Joint measurability is supplied by F:Kernel(A×B)B, not by a hidden theorem hypothesis. The same R appears in hF and μ⊗ₘR. No project-owned alias, representative choice, extra standing instance or measurability certificate for the good-fiber predicate appears.

conclusion.original: L, retaining a and updating b through F(a,b), is reversible under ν=μ⊗ₘR.
conclusion.reconstructed: For every measurable joint U,V, ∫_U K(x,V)dπ=∫_V K(x,U)dπ, allowing both sides infinite.
conclusion.evidence: Invariance.lean:60–62 is exactly the reconstructed nonnegative flux equality. deterministic_prod_apply' gives L((a,b),T)=F(a,b)(T_a) for every measurable joint T. The helper computes arbitrary-joint-set flux by indicator integration, and lintegral_congr_ae applies the assumed fiber equality. No subtraction or signed integral occurs.
